text: Schedule F was created by an executive order in October 2020, revoked in 2021, and restored by executive order on January 20, 2025. It lets career federal employees in policy-influencing jobs be reclassified so they can be dismissed like political appointees.
src_label: Federal Register (Executive Office of the President document) (10/26/2020); The White House (January 20, 2025); govinfo.gov (U.S. Government Publishing Office, Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents) (October 21, 2020); Trump White House Archives (trumpwhitehouse.archives.gov) (October 21, 2020); United States Government Publishing Office (govinfo.gov), Daily Compilation of Presidential Documents (January 20, 2025)

sources.publisherFull: Federal Register (Executive Office of the President document)
quotes: Executive Order 13957 of October 21, 2020 Creating Schedule F in the Excepted Service

Schedule F. Positions of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character not normally subject to change as a result of a Presidential transition shall be listed in Schedule F.

Except as required by statute, the Civil Service Rules and Regulations shall not apply to removals from positions listed in Schedules A, C, D, E, or F, or from positions excepted from the competitive service by statute.
Agencies need the flexibility to expeditiously remove poorly performing employees from these positions without facing extensive delays or litigation.

Executive Order 13957 of October 21, 2020 (Creating Schedule F in the Excepted Service), is hereby immediately reinstated with full force and effect, subject to the amendments described in section 3 of this order; provided that the date of this order shall be treated as the date of Executive Order 13957.

Executive Order 14003 of January 22, 2021 (Protecting the Federal Workforce), is hereby revoked, and any rules, regulations, guidance, or other agency policies effectuated under Executive Order 14003 shall not be enforced.
beginning with positions of a confidential, policy-determining, policy-making, or policy-advocating character.

quotes: Using artificial intelligence, the towers continuously monitor wherever is needed, sorting out what are real concerns and what comes back as a false positive.
